title: DNA language models are powerful predictors of genome-wide variant effects

nodes.text: The Genomic Pre-trained Network (GPN) is a multispecies DNA language model trained by self-supervised masked-nucleotide prediction on unaligned reference genomes, learning genome-wide variant effects, gene structure, and DNA motifs without supervision.
nodes.evidence: we here introduce the Genomic Pre-trained Network (GPN), a model designed to learn genome-wide variant effects through unsupervised pretraining on genomic DNA sequences

nodes.text: GPN uses a convolutional neural network with dilated convolutions that processes a 512-bp masked DNA sequence (15% of positions masked during training) and outputs four nucleotide probabilities per masked position, trained with cross-entropy loss on the reference sequence.
nodes.evidence: The sequence is processed through a convolutional neural network resulting in a high-dimensional contextual embedding ... a final layer outputs four nucleotide probabilities at each masked position

nodes.text: The GPN variant effect prediction score is defined as the log-likelihood ratio between the alternate and reference allele at a masked variant position.
nodes.evidence: The GPN variant effect prediction score is defined as the log-likelihood ratio between the alternate and reference allele

nodes.text: GPN outperforms genome-wide conservation-based predictors such as phyloP and phastCons, which rely on whole-genome alignments of closely related species.
nodes.evidence: GPN outperforms genome-wide conservation scores such as phyloP and phastCons, which rely on whole-genome alignments of 18 closely related species

nodes.text: Unlike prior DNA language models (refs 23-29) which had not demonstrated accurate self-supervised variant effect prediction, GPN provides a unified approach capable of accurate unsupervised genome-wide variant effect prediction.
nodes.evidence: While existing DNA language models (23-29) have not yet demonstrated the ability to make accurate variant effect predictions based on self-supervision alone, GPN presents a unified approach

nodes.text: Unlike supervised functional-genomics approaches such as DeepSEA, Enformer, and Sei, GPN requires only DNA sequence and no expensive functional genomics data, so it can be applied to any species with a reference genome.
nodes.evidence: this approach's success depends on the availability of high-quality functional genomics data ... which can be prohibitively expensive ... Our model, trained solely on DNA sequences, can be applied to any species with a reference genome

nodes.text: Unlike variant-type-specific models (e.g. for missense or regulatory variants only), GPN's genome-wide scores allow prioritization across different variant types, which is needed for fine-mapping and polygenic scores.
nodes.evidence: a model that is exclusively designed for either missense or regulatory variants would not be able to prioritize between a de novo missense variant and a de novo promoter variant

nodes.text: Trained without supervision, GPN's contextual embeddings cluster genomic windows by region type, and a logistic regression on these embeddings classifies gene regions with up to 96% accuracy on CDS (lowest 51% on ncRNA), far exceeding k-mer frequency baselines.
nodes.evidence: achieving the highest accuracy on CDS (96%) and the lowest on ncRNA (51%) ... This level of classification accuracy cannot be achieved merely through k-mer frequencies

nodes.text: GPN's prediction confidence tracks expected functional constraint: perplexity is significantly lower at splice donors/acceptors, start/stop codons, and codon positions CDS2 < CDS1 < CDS3, than in intergenic and intronic regions.
nodes.evidence: Perplexity in CDS2 is significantly smaller than that in CDS1, which in turn is significantly smaller than that in CDS3 (all Mann-Whitney P-values < 10^-300)

nodes.text: Adapting TF-MoDISco to GPN scores in promoter regions identified about 160 motifs, some matching known PlantTFDB transcription factor binding sites and others potentially novel promoter elements.
nodes.evidence: Applying the adapted TF-MoDISco to GPN scores in promoter regions, we identified approximately a hundred and sixty motifs

nodes.text: In silico mutagenesis rankings by GPN score are consistent with established deleteriousness, with splice donor, splice acceptor, stop gained, and start lost as the four lowest-scored variant types, and missense predicted more impactful than synonymous.
nodes.evidence: the four lowest scored variant types are splice donor, splice acceptor, stop gained, and start lost variants

nodes.text: Down-weighting the training loss on repetitive elements improved test perplexity in nonrepetitive regions and reduced spurious low scores for repeat variants from 27% (no down-weighting) to 8-9% ranking before the first decile of missense variants.
nodes.evidence: in models with 0.0 and 0.1 down-weighting, respectively, 8% and 9% of repeat variants are ranked before the first decile of missense variants ... a substantial decrease compared to the 27% observed in the model without any down-weighting

nodes.text: GPN was trained on A. thaliana plus seven related Brassicales species and achieves state-of-the-art genome-wide variant effect prediction in Arabidopsis thaliana, a model plant organism also relevant to human disease.
nodes.evidence: achieving state-of-the-art performance in Arabidopsis thaliana, a model organism for plant biology and a source of insight into human diseases
